campos.descripcion: Install the exact current Three.js release with npm for bundler projects. If a browser CDN is unavoidable use an import map pinned to the same exact release instead of a floating URL.
campos.hacer: Pin three@0.185.1 and keep core and addon imports on that release
campos.no_hacer: Use a floating latest URL or a legacy global build as the default production setup

campos.descripcion: CapsuleGeometry is part of the current Three.js geometry API and directly creates a capsule from radius length cap segments and radial segments.
campos.hacer: Construct current capsule meshes with THREE.CapsuleGeometry
campos.no_hacer: Rebuild a standard capsule from separate cylinder and sphere meshes unless custom topology is required

campos.descripcion: OrbitControls is an addon and must be imported explicitly from the three/addons path while the core library is imported from three.
campos.hacer: Import the named OrbitControls addon before constructing controls
campos.no_hacer: Expect THREE.OrbitControls to exist on the core namespace

campos.descripcion: When OrbitControls cannot be loaded implement spherical orbit using mousedown/mousemove/mouseup. The key is rotating in spherical coordinates so both horizontal AND vertical drag work correctly.
campos.hacer: Rotate camera in spherical coordinates so both axes respond correctly to drag
campos.no_hacer: Move camera.position.x directly — vertical drag is silently ignored and the orbit is incorrect

campos.tema: Use ESM Imports with Bundlers or Import Maps
campos.descripcion: Import Three.js from three in bundler projects. For a no-build browser page define an exact-version import map for three and three/addons/ before importing modules.
campos.hacer: Use one ESM dependency graph with core and addons pinned to the same release
campos.no_hacer: Mix global script builds with ES module imports or map core and addons to different versions

campos.descripcion: Create one WebGLRenderer instance for the lifetime of the page. Multiple renderers compete for the browser GPU context limit (8–16 contexts) and cause context-lost errors especially on mobile.
campos.hacer: Reuse a single renderer and swap scene content instead of recreating the renderer
campos.no_hacer: Create a new renderer on each component mount or scene transition

campos.descripcion: Cap devicePixelRatio at 2. Retina displays report 3x or higher. Going from 2x to 3x multiplies pixel count by 2.25x with no visible quality improvement at normal viewing distance.
campos.hacer: Apply Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2) — cap is at 2 not at 3
campos.no_hacer: Pass window.devicePixelRatio directly without any cap

campos.descripcion: Set alpha:true on the renderer and control the background color through CSS rather than a renderer clear color. This composites the canvas correctly over any HTML content behind it.
campos.hacer: Set alpha:true on renderer and let body or a parent div provide the background color
campos.no_hacer: Set a solid renderer clear color when the canvas must composite over HTML behind it

campos.descripcion: Always update camera.aspect and call camera.updateProjectionMatrix() inside every resize handler. A stale aspect ratio causes the entire scene to appear stretched or squashed horizontally.
campos.hacer: Update camera.aspect then call updateProjectionMatrix() on every resize
campos.no_hacer: Let aspect ratio become stale after the browser window changes size

campos.descripcion: Use a field of view between 45 and 75 degrees. Below 45 creates compressed telephoto distortion. Above 90 creates visible fisheye distortion at frame edges.
campos.hacer: Start at 75 for general interactive scenes; use 45–55 for product close-ups
campos.no_hacer: Use FOV above 90 or below 30 without a deliberate artistic reason

campos.descripcion: Always set an explicit camera position and call camera.lookAt() before the first render. The default camera at the origin pointing down -Z makes subjects at arbitrary coordinates invisible or tiny.
campos.hacer: Set camera.position.set() and camera.lookAt() to frame the subject before the first render
campos.no_hacer: Leave the camera at default position (0 0 0) with no lookAt — subject may be behind the camera or microscopic

campos.descripcion: Use OrbitControls for model viewers and exploratory scenes where the user needs free-look. Use a GSAP scroll-driven camera rig for product reveals or storytelling where the camera path must stay fixed.
campos.hacer: Import OrbitControls from three/addons and match the camera control approach to the scene's UX intent
campos.no_hacer: Use OrbitControls for a scripted reveal where users can orbit away before it completes

campos.descripcion: Creating a new geometry inside animate() allocates a fresh GPU buffer every frame and exhausts VRAM within seconds. Create all geometry exactly once before the loop starts. Use attribute mutation if positions must change per frame.
campos.hacer: Create all geometry before the animation loop; mutate BufferAttribute arrays in-place if needed
campos.no_hacer: Call any new XxxGeometry() constructor inside the animation loop

campos.descripcion: When multiple objects share the same shape create one geometry instance and pass it to every Mesh. Each Mesh gets its own transform and material while all share a single GPU buffer.
campos.hacer: Create one geometry and pass the same reference to every Mesh constructor
campos.no_hacer: Create a separate identical geometry inside a loop for each object

campos.descripcion: Call geometry.dispose() and material.dispose() and texture.dispose() for every texture map when removing objects from the scene. Three.js never releases GPU resources automatically — they stay in VRAM until explicitly freed.
campos.hacer: Dispose of geometry + material + every texture map before calling scene.remove()
campos.no_hacer: Call scene.remove() alone without any dispose calls

campos.descripcion: Use the minimum segment count that achieves the desired silhouette quality. Hero objects: 32–64 segments. Background objects: 8–16. Particle stand-ins: 6–8. High counts on background geometry waste GPU draw calls with zero visible benefit.
campos.hacer: Apply a tiered segment budget based on the visual priority of each object in the scene
campos.no_hacer: Default every sphere and cylinder to 64+ segments regardless of its role

campos.descripcion: For custom shapes use BufferGeometry with typed BufferAttribute data for positions normals colors and other vertex attributes.
campos.hacer: Use THREE.BufferGeometry with Float32Array-backed attributes for custom vertex data
campos.no_hacer: Reference or instantiate the removed THREE.Geometry class

campos.descripcion: MeshBasicMaterial ignores all lights and is significantly cheaper — use it for UI overlays HUDs and flat-colored decorative elements. MeshStandardMaterial is PBR-accurate and requires lights. Never use StandardMaterial where BasicMaterial suffices.
campos.hacer: Use MeshBasicMaterial for any object that does not need lighting; use MeshStandardMaterial for physical objects
campos.no_hacer: Apply MeshStandardMaterial to flat UI elements that never receive light — lights still run for them

campos.descripcion: Share one material instance across all meshes that have identical properties. Call mat.clone() only when individual meshes genuinely need different property values. Duplicate materials waste GPU VRAM.
campos.hacer: Assign the same material reference to all meshes with identical visual properties
campos.no_hacer: Create a new material inside a loop for objects that look identical

campos.descripcion: Textures are the single largest consumer of GPU VRAM in most Three.js scenes. Call texture.dispose() when switching scenes or removing objects — Three.js does not garbage-collect GPU resources automatically.
campos.hacer: Track all loaded textures and call dispose() on each one during scene teardown or on object removal
campos.no_hacer: Load textures without any cleanup path — they persist in VRAM for the entire page lifetime

campos.descripcion: Any scene using MeshStandardMaterial or MeshPhongMaterial requires at minimum one AmbientLight (fill) and one DirectionalLight (shading direction). Without both the objects render as solid black — the material is there but no light reaches it.
campos.hacer: Add AmbientLight for fill and DirectionalLight for shading whenever PBR or Phong materials are used
campos.no_hacer: Use MeshStandardMaterial without adding any lights to the scene

campos.descripcion: renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true must be set before any castShadow or receiveShadow flags. Without it the shadow map is never allocated and all shadow flags are silently ignored.
campos.hacer: Set renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true first then set castShadow and receiveShadow on lights and meshes
campos.no_hacer: Set castShadow on a light or mesh without enabling renderer.shadowMap.enabled — shadows never render

campos.descripcion: Shadow map rendering redraws the entire scene from the light's perspective every frame. Enable castShadow only on the primary directional light and receiveShadow only on hero meshes and the ground plane.
campos.hacer: Enable shadows only on the key light and the most important meshes
campos.no_hacer: Enable castShadow and receiveShadow on every object in the scene including particles

campos.descripcion: MeshBasicMaterial completely ignores all scene lights. Adding lights solely to illuminate BasicMaterial objects wastes a light pass on every frame with zero visible effect.
campos.hacer: Omit lights entirely when every material in the scene is MeshBasicMaterial
campos.no_hacer: Add AmbientLight and DirectionalLight to a scene that uses only MeshBasicMaterial

campos.descripcion: Create exactly one Raycaster instance outside all event handlers. Store mouse coordinates in pointermove (cheap). Call setFromCamera and intersectObjects together inside the animate() loop — once per frame instead of once per mouse event.
campos.hacer: Create one Raycaster; store mouse in pointermove; call setFromCamera + intersectObjects inside animate()
campos.no_hacer: Create a new THREE.Raycaster() inside a mousemove handler or call setFromCamera inside the event listener

campos.descripcion: Raycasting requires mouse in Normalized Device Coordinates: X from -1 (left) to +1 (right) and Y from +1 (top) to -1 (bottom). The Y axis is inverted relative to screen space. A missing negation on Y causes all raycasts to miss or hit the wrong objects.
campos.hacer: Apply the full NDC formula — including the negation on the Y axis
campos.no_hacer: Forget to negate Y — raycasting appears to work but hits objects mirrored vertically

campos.descripcion: Call raycaster.setFromCamera(mouse camera) and then raycaster.intersectObjects(targets true) inside the animate() loop. setFromCamera must come before intersectObjects every frame — without it the raycaster uses a stale ray direction.
campos.hacer: Call setFromCamera then intersectObjects in order inside every animate() frame
campos.no_hacer: Call intersectObjects without calling setFromCamera first — the raycaster uses a stale or zero ray

campos.tema: Recursive Flag for Groups and GLTF
campos.descripcion: Pass true as the second argument to intersectObjects when testing Groups or GLTF loaded models. Geometry lives on child Mesh objects — without recursive:true the parent group is tested but has no geometry and hits is always empty.
campos.hacer: Use intersectObjects(targets true) for Groups or any loaded model
campos.no_hacer: Raycast against a parent Group without the recursive flag

campos.descripcion: Set document.body.style.cursor = 'pointer' when intersections are found and reset to 'auto' when none are found. Without cursor feedback users cannot discover that 3D objects are interactive.
campos.hacer: Update cursor to pointer on hit; reset to auto on miss in the same animate loop block
campos.no_hacer: Run raycasting and read hits without ever updating the cursor style

campos.descripcion: Drive the render loop exclusively with requestAnimationFrame or renderer.setAnimationLoop(). Never use setInterval or setTimeout — they are not synchronized to the display refresh rate and keep running when the tab is hidden draining battery.
campos.hacer: Use requestAnimationFrame or renderer.setAnimationLoop() as the sole render loop driver
campos.no_hacer: Use setInterval or setTimeout for render timing

campos.descripcion: Use THREE.Clock and clock.getDelta() for all time-based motion. A hardcoded increment like += 0.01 runs at 2x speed on 120Hz displays and at unpredictable speed when frames drop under load. CRITICAL: call getDelta() exactly ONCE per animate() frame and store the result in a local dt variable. getDelta() resets the internal clock on every call — a second call in the same frame always returns ~0, silently breaking any animation block that uses it.
campos.hacer: Call clock.getDelta() once at the top of animate(); store result in dt; reuse dt everywhere in that frame
campos.no_hacer: Call clock.getDelta() more than once per frame or inside a helper called from animate()

campos.descripcion: Use value += (target - value) * alpha each frame to smoothly interpolate toward a moving target. An alpha of 0.03–0.1 produces organic easing for camera follow pointer-tracking and hover scale effects without requiring GSAP.
campos.hacer: Apply the lerp formula each frame with a small alpha for smooth organic motion
campos.no_hacer: Snap a value directly to the target producing an instant jarring jump

campos.descripcion: Use GSAP timelines for any animation with more than two sequential steps or for scroll-linked camera paths. GSAP timelines can be paused reversed and scrubbed — far more maintainable than boolean state machines.
campos.hacer: Use GSAP timelines for sequences with more than two steps and for scroll-driven animations
campos.no_hacer: Implement multi-step sequences with boolean flags and manual frame counters

campos.tema: Pause Render Loop on Tab Hidden
campos.descripcion: Use renderer.setAnimationLoop() as the loop driver so you can pass null to pause and a function to resume. Continuous rendering in a hidden tab wastes CPU GPU and battery with no user benefit.
campos.hacer: Use renderer.setAnimationLoop(animate) to drive the loop; pass null to pause on visibilitychange
campos.no_hacer: Drive with internal requestAnimationFrame and never stop the loop when the tab is hidden

campos.descripcion: Load GSAP from its own CDN script tag before your scene script. In bundler projects install via npm and import. GSAP is a completely separate library from Three.js — never try to import it from the Three.js package.
campos.hacer: Load GSAP CDN before the scene script; or npm install gsap and import separately
campos.no_hacer: Import gsap from three or expect it to be defined without a separate load

campos.descripcion: Call gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger) once at the top of your script before any scrollTrigger config object. Without registration the ScrollTrigger name is undefined and the tween throws immediately.
campos.hacer: Call gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger) as the first line before any gsap.to/from/timeline with scrollTrigger
campos.no_hacer: Include scrollTrigger config in gsap.to() calls without first registering the plugin

campos.descripcion: GSAP can tween any numeric JavaScript property including mesh.position.x mesh.rotation.y and material.opacity. No wrapper or adaptor is needed. Note: to tween material.opacity the material must have transparent:true set before the tween starts.
campos.hacer: Pass Three.js object properties directly to gsap.to(); set transparent:true before tweening opacity
campos.no_hacer: Use a plain proxy object then manually copy values to Three.js properties every frame

campos.descripcion: Use scrub:true or scrub:1 to link camera movement continuously to scroll position as a 0–1 ratio. scrub:1 adds a 1-second lag for cinematic smoothness. onEnter/onLeave fire only once and create jarring snaps — not the right tool for a camera path.
campos.hacer: Use scrub:1 for any scroll-controlled camera movement
campos.no_hacer: Use onEnter or onLeave callbacks for camera motion — they snap instead of scrubbing

campos.descripcion: Use THREE.InstancedMesh when rendering 50 or more identical objects. It submits all N transforms in one draw call instead of N draw calls and reduces CPU-GPU communication overhead dramatically.
campos.hacer: Use InstancedMesh for any group of 50+ meshes sharing the same geometry and material
campos.no_hacer: Create 50+ separate Mesh objects with the same geometry and material

campos.tema: Tone Mapping and Output Color Space
campos.descripcion: Three.js color management is enabled by default. Keep working colors in the linear-sRGB space and set the renderer output color space to SRGBColorSpace; choose tone mapping when rendering HDR lighting to a display.
campos.hacer: Use the default ColorManagement.enabled state and set renderer.outputColorSpace plus an appropriate toneMapping
campos.no_hacer: Disable color management or use removed outputEncoding and sRGBEncoding properties

campos.descripcion: The antialias option can only be set at WebGLRenderer construction time. Setting renderer.antialias after construction has absolutely no effect — the WebGL context is already created without it. Decide before instantiating.
campos.hacer: Set antialias:true inside the WebGLRenderer constructor options object
campos.no_hacer: Construct the renderer without antialias then try to enable it by assigning the property

campos.tema: FogExp2 for Depth and Far Culling
campos.descripcion: Use scene.fog to create atmospheric depth. As a secondary benefit objects that disappear into fog before the far plane stop contributing to draw calls — useful in scenes with large view distances.
campos.hacer: Add FogExp2 to scenes with view distances above 100 units for both visual atmosphere and implicit far culling
campos.no_hacer: Ignore fog in scenes with far:1000+ and many distant objects that contribute tiny pixels per draw call

campos.tema: BufferGeometry Plus Points for Particle Systems
campos.descripcion: Build all particle systems with BufferGeometry plus a Float32Array position attribute rendered as Points. Never use individual Mesh objects as particles — they cannot scale past a few hundred with good performance.
campos.hacer: Use Points plus BufferGeometry for all particle effects
campos.no_hacer: Create hundreds of individual Mesh objects to simulate a particle system

campos.descripcion: Start particle systems at 1000–3000 particles. Beyond 50000 causes sustained frame drops on mid-range mobile. Always test on a real device before increasing the count — desktop and mobile GPU performance ratios can be 10:1.
campos.hacer: Start at 3000 particles and profile on actual mobile hardware before raising the limit
campos.no_hacer: Set particle count at 100000 or higher without any mobile profiling

campos.descripcion: After mutating any BufferAttribute array values per frame you must set geometry.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true so Three.js re-uploads the changed buffer to the GPU. Without it the GPU still uses the old data and particles appear completely frozen.
campos.hacer: Set needsUpdate = true on the position attribute after every per-frame mutation of the array
campos.no_hacer: Mutate the Float32Array values without flagging needsUpdate — positions update in JS but not on the GPU

campos.descripcion: Size the renderer and camera to the canvas element's clientWidth and clientHeight — not window.innerWidth and innerHeight. This is correct when the canvas is inside a flex or grid container that does not fill the full viewport.
campos.hacer: Use canvas.clientWidth and canvas.clientHeight for all renderer and camera sizing
campos.no_hacer: Hardcode renderer size to window.innerWidth/innerHeight when the canvas may be inside a container

campos.descripcion: Use ResizeObserver on the canvas container instead of the window resize event. ResizeObserver fires when the container element changes size independently of the browser window — common in split-pane layouts and sidebar collapsing.
campos.hacer: Attach ResizeObserver to the canvas parent element for accurate container-aware resize detection
campos.no_hacer: Use only window.addEventListener('resize') for canvas sizing when the canvas is not fullscreen

campos.descripcion: Add touchstart and touchmove listeners alongside mouse events so the scene remains interactive on mobile. Normalize touch coordinates to the same NDC range as mouse events and pass passive:false on touchmove if you call preventDefault.
campos.hacer: Handle both mouse and touch input for any interactive 3D scene
campos.no_hacer: Add only mouse event listeners and leave touch users with no interaction

campos.descripcion: Check window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') before starting any auto-rotation, particle animation, or camera movement. Users who enable this OS preference have motion sickness or vestibular disorders. IMPORTANT: reading .matches once at page load is a one-time snapshot — if the user changes their OS accessibility setting mid-session the scene will not react. Attach a 'change' listener to the MediaQueryList so noMotion stays in sync at runtime.
campos.hacer: Use matchMedia.addEventListener('change') to keep noMotion reactive; gate all auto-animation on the live value
campos.no_hacer: Read .matches once at startup and never update it — the scene ignores mid-session OS setting changes

campos.descripcion: Add role='img' and a descriptive aria-label to renderer.domElement after appending it to the DOM. Screen readers receive no information from a WebGL canvas — the aria-label is the only description they can announce to users.
campos.hacer: Set role='img' and a meaningful aria-label on renderer.domElement before or after appending it
campos.no_hacer: Append the canvas to the DOM with no accessibility attributes — invisible to screen readers

campos.descripcion: For production install the exact Three.js release from npm and use a bundler such as Vite. Import optional loaders controls and post-processing modules from three/addons so all modules share one version.
campos.hacer: Use npm install three@0.185.1 and import core plus addons through ESM
campos.no_hacer: Serve legacy global scripts or import addons from deprecated examples/js paths

campos.descripcion: Load 3D models using GLTFLoader and traverse gltf.scene to configure castShadow receiveShadow and material overrides on all child Mesh nodes. Calling scene.add(gltf.scene) alone silently skips all shadow and material configuration.
campos.hacer: Use GLTFLoader and traverse the entire gltf.scene graph to set up shadows and materials on every Mesh child
campos.no_hacer: Load a GLTF model and pass gltf.scene directly to scene.add without traversing child meshes

campos.descripcion: Use THREE.LOD to automatically swap high-detail and low-detail geometry as objects move closer or farther from the camera. This maintains frame rate in scenes with many objects spread across a large depth range.
campos.hacer: Use THREE.LOD to reduce triangle count on distant objects automatically
campos.no_hacer: Render the same high-polygon geometry for every object regardless of its distance from the camera
